syzygy_checkpoint: The commit containing this artifact includes the complete native and public syzygy implementation, tests and CI selection.
objective: Implement general prime-field quotient inversion, complete minimal polynomials and complete polynomial relation modules through independently checked native operations and retained-source Python boundaries.

implementation.inverse: The complete augmented ideal I+<f> determines invertibility, including positive-dimensional quotients. Checked Bezout cofactors supply an inverse reduced in the declared order; a separate signed convolution checks the original identity and reduced remainder. A proved proper augmented ideal establishes noninvertibility.
implementation.minimal_polynomial: Complete elimination of the original variables from <I,t-f> yields the annihilator ideal in GF(p)[t]. Independent exact source binding and coefficient checks establish its monic generator, including inseparable and nilpotent multiplicities. An empty elimination ideal proves transcendence; the unit ideal returns one.
implementation.syzygies: A complete Groebner certificate supplies G=A*F, F=B*G and strict standard representations of every S-pair. All nonzero rows of I-B*A and S*A generate the complete relation module on the original ordered inputs. A separate signed coefficient checker requires every row and checks each zero dot product. Zero, duplicate and scaled coordinates remain distinct.
implementation.performance_structure: Syzygy composition accumulates products into existing sparse rows without repeatedly cloning the target. All operations reuse the established bounded ideal/elimination kernels and reference arithmetic; no new dependency or rational fallback was added.
implementation.python: GroebnerBasis.invert, minimal_polynomial/minpoly and syzygies retain exact typed sources, original field, coefficient policies and container/held-node snapshots through admission, native checking and lifting. Only a verified nonunit becomes NotInvertible and only a verified zero annihilator ideal becomes None.
implementation.boundary_repair: Original sources are snapshotted before implicit Dummy creation in both GF(p) and QQ minimal-polynomial requests, preventing a mutation during parameter construction from becoming the accepted original input.

limitations: A syzygy result is a complete generating set, not necessarily a minimal set or a reduced module Groebner basis.
Resource, degree, source and output bounds can refuse otherwise valid mathematical requests; failures remain terminal and are not reported as noninvertibility or transcendence.
Extension fields, multivariate factorization/GCD/resultants/composition and broader compatibility remain outside this slice.
These are scoped in-process independently checked receipts, not portable proof-kernel certificates or a certified compatibility profile.
